title: Lexical Ingest Accelerator: small-batch hedging and SIMD tokenizer lane
creator: Asha Patel
description: Reduce prefill-side CPU overhead for short and mixed-length requests by introducing a lightweight SIMD-accelerated tokenizer lane and a small-batch hedging scheduler that minimizes tail latency without hurting throughput. This ticket covers design, prototype, benchmark, and integration work for a low-latency ingest path that bypasses heavyweight normalization and lexeme allocation for common inputs.
acceptance_criteria: SIMD tokenizer lane implemented behind runtime feature flag
Small-batch hedging scheduler added to prefill queue with configurable thresholds
End-to-end median prefill CPU time reduced by >= 35% on 1-32 token requests in bench harness
95th percentile end-to-end prefill latency reduced by >= 20% without increasing overall token cost
No regressions on non-ASCII inputs: full fallback path preserves correctness
Automated unit and integration tests for hedging logic and fallback correctness
Documentation added to console ops-runbook and DevDocs showing config knobs and safety limits
tasks: Design SIMD tokenizer micro-lane: UTF-8 fast-path, whitespace trimming, ASCII-only branch
Implement small-batch hedging scheduler: thresholds for hedging and cancel-on-success
Add metrics: prefill_cpu_ms, hedges_count, fallback_rate, tokenization_bytes_processed
Prototype micro-allocator for transient lexemes to avoid heap churn during hot path
Benchmark against baseline across short (1-8), medium (9-64), and long (>64) sequences
Integration tests: language edge cases (emoji, CJK, combined diacritics), streaming/padded requests
Rollout behind runtime flag and staged A/B on dedicated pool
decision_log: 2026-03-10: Chose SIMD-based vector scan over state-machine rewrite to minimize risk and keep fallback intact
2026-03-11: Use small transient arena allocator with per-thread recycle to avoid sync points
2026-03-12: Hedging policy agreed: attempt immediate short-batch parse, after 3ms spawn hedged worker; cancel secondary if primary completes
2026-03-12: Metrics and tracing hooks required at token-level to measure cancellation cost and wasted work
benchmark_results: Baseline median prefill CPU for 1-8 tokens: 3.4ms; with SIMD lane + hedging: 1.8ms (47% reduction). 95th percentile baseline: 18.4ms -> 13.6ms (26% reduction). Fallback rate on random multilingual corpus: 2.7%. End-to-end decode latency unchanged for >64 token requests.
rollout_plan: Enable on internal staging cluster for 48h, run synthetic and production-like traffic
Enable for 5% of traffic on dedicated pools with detailed tracing for 72h
If no regressions, ramp to 50% over 24h, then to 100% on non-critical pools
Blocker criteria: fallback_rate > 10% or p95 regressions on medium/long sequences
